clue.text: Historical learning aids formerly used in Sunday School

indicators.note: the word for formerly is placed within the two abbreviations, as if put to use inside them

parts.note: late can mean formerly, as in 'the late chairman'

explanation.surface: Old classroom equipment once found in church Sunday schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Children once wrote lessons on small framed boards of grey stone, a schoolroom tool now long gone.

clue.text: Make solo trip with me in the city

indicators.note: make tells us to form something new out of the following letters, rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to travel alone with the speaker into town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' signals rearranging SOLOTRIP plus ME; 'with' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, important urban centre is a city, often the chief one of a region.

clue.text: Nancy, famous MP, accommodated by friend in country

indicators.note: something accommodated by another is housed within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pal is a friend
Nancy Astor was the first woman to take her seat in the British House of Commons

explanation.surface: A celebrated female politician is put up by a friend out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, the clue word describes rural scenes and farmland life, just like the answer.

clue.text: Overflowing with good spirits and champagne

definitions.meaning: describing a lively, effervescent, cheerful person
informal name for sparkling wine, from its fizz

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from fizzing: a cheerful effervescent personality and a sparkling wine.

clue.text: Foot soldiers start trouble in cellar

parts.note: the foot of something is its base
men is a common word for soldiers

indicators.note: the start of the word trouble means only its opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Infantry begin causing a disturbance down in the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot soldiers' reads as one phrase meaning infantry, but it has to be split into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is a room below ground level, which is what a basement is: a synonym.

clue.text: Individual kept in place by escort is a poet

indicators.note: one word is held in position within another, so it goes inside

parts.note: to escort someone somewhere is to bring them
own means individual or particular to oneself

explanation.surface: A single person held in position by a chaperone turns out to be a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning was a Victorian English poet, an example of the class named.

clue.text: Immoral, not missing love after ten years

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word following the ten-year period in the answer

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years

indicators.note: missing means the zero-shaped letter for love drops out of the word not

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shown as the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone has been immoral without missing their lover for a whole decade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes the O out of the clue's own word, leaving two letters that go after the decade.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes self-indulgent moral decline, so it serves as a synonym for immoral.

clue.text: A letter turned up in this jacket

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: a note is a short letter

explanation.surface: A letter is found when the pocket of this jacket is turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in this' links the wordplay to the definition, pointing at the jacket named by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A short black jacket was worn by pupils of the famous English public school, so it names a jacket style.

clue.text: Mongrel locked in dirty kennel

indicators.note: the answer is enclosed within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A mutt shut away in a filthy dog house.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyke is an informal word for a mongrel dog, a dialect synonym.

clue.text: Strong drinks won't keep your legs warm

definitions.meaning: small measures of spirits, as opposed to long drinks
cryptic hint at short trousers that leave the legs bare

explanation.definitionFit: Spirits served in small measures are one sense; knee-length trousers that expose the legs are the other.

clue.text: Ornamental designs in pine industry

parts.note: to pine is to fret or worry
industry means hard work

explanation.surface: Decorative patterns carved in pine wood by a manufacturing firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the wood used for carving, but here it is the verb meaning fret.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretwork is decorative openwork carving or patterning, an example of ornamental design.

clue.text: My family's mourner removes dangerous explosives

parts.note: mine can mean my family, as in 'me and mine', so its possessive is mine's
a weeper is one who mourns

explanation.surface: A grieving relative of mine turns out to be clearing bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what the answer does: a ship that clears sea mines.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval vessel whose job is clearing sea-mines is described by what it does with those explosives.

clue.text: Specialist holds hands after one attempt

indicators.note: holds means the specialist word contains the other letters

parts.note: an expert is a specialist

indicators.note: after puts the workers following the numeral for one

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
hands are workers, men

explanation.surface: An expert takes on workers after one failed try.
explanation.definitionFit: An experiment is a trial or test, so it can stand for an attempt.

clue.text: Lose sight of timid people getting nasty slap in the middle

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed in the centre of the other word

parts.note: timid people are figuratively mice

indicators.note: nasty suggests something messed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shy folk lose track after a vicious slap lands among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges SLAP to SPLA, which goes into the middle of MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To misplace something is to lose track of where it is, synonymous with losing sight of it.

clue.text: No bunker could be perfectly even

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A golf course with no sand trap might be perfectly flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface that is unbroken has no gaps or bumps, hence completely even.

clue.text: No dram preserves doctor like some paint

indicators.note: preserves means one word holds and keeps the other inside

parts.note: a nip is a small dram of spirits

explanation.surface: A small drink that keeps a doctor going, in decorating terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Some paint is formulated so it does not run, described with this hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Bank keeps one hundred — just

indicators.note: keeps means one word holds the other within it

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
cent is from the Latin for a hundred, as in per cent

explanation.surface: A bank has only just kept a hundred in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a financial noun but is the verb, as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Just, in the sense of a short while ago, is a synonym of the adverb.

clue.text: Flower girl's ill with collar put back around

indicators.note: around tells us the reversed word wraps itself round the other
put back means the word for collar is reversed

parts.note: to collar a culprit is to nail them, arrest them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flower girl is sick with a collar fastened round her backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' gives LIAN; the clue's 's reads as 'has', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lillian is a girl's name derived from the lily, so it is a flower-based girl's name.

clue.text: Amusing person, not so sweet as a cheat

parts.note: a card is a joker, an amusing character
sharper is the comparative of sharp, the opposite of sweet in taste

explanation.surface: A funny fellow, less sweet in nature, as a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharper is a professional swindler at card games, a type of cheat.

clue.text: Prejudice exists to break up a masterpiece

indicators.note: the word for exists splits the other piece apart by going into it

parts.note: a gem is a fine piece of work, a masterpiece
is means exists

explanation.surface: Bias exists to destroy a great work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is discrimination against people on grounds of age, a form of prejudice.

clue.text: Move slowly wearing check

parts.note: you are in clothes you are wearing
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Creeping along dressed in a checked garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to edge forward a tiny distance at a time, synonym of moving slowly.

clue.text: Mark's machine

parts.note: the apostrophe-s gives a letter S
a car is a machine, often colloquially

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark owns a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' reads as a man's name, but it is the definition, a blemish; its 's gives the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting mark left on the skin by a wound, a synonym.

clue.text: Diminutive celebrity goes to prison

indicators.note: goes to says the celebrity word joins the end of the prison word

parts.note: nick is British slang for a prison or police station
a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A star is jailed for a minor offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diminutive' looks like an adjective meaning small, but it is the noun: a shortened form of a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A diminutive is a short or pet form of a name, which is a kind of informal name.

clue.text: Comment about a Gospel

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Mark is one of the four Gospels

explanation.surface: A remark concerning one of the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a spoken or written observation, synonymous with a comment.

clue.text: Cut up fish in a rush

parts.note: cut up can mean distressed or hurt
ling is a long-bodied sea fish

explanation.surface: Slicing a fish up in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurtling means moving at great speed, an equivalent of going in a rush.

clue.text: One with rigid behind

parts.note: a means one
stern means strict or rigid

explanation.surface: A person with an inflexible backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a noun for a backside but is the adverb: at the back of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical term for at or toward the rear of a ship, meaning behind.
